summary: Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from Mahidol University by 2021, supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.

Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903 and held posts as a lecturer at Kyoto University (circa 1908–1923) and professor at Otani University in 1915.

Enichi Ocho (1906–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa between circa 1926 and 1931. He was a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture (1931) and professor emeritus at Otani University.

Enryo Inoue (1858–1919) was a philosopher and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a BA and doctorate at the University of Tokyo studying under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara, and later founded and taught at Toyo University.

Ensho Kanakura (1896–1987) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After earning his doctorate at the University of Tokyo in 1931, he was a professor at Tohoku University (circa 1926–1959), Miyagi University of Education (1967), and Rissho University.
Ensho Nasu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Ryukoku University (attested 1996), where he was supervised by Esho Mikogami and taught by Kei Mikogami.

Enshu Kurumiya (born 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 1974 and served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a Tibetologist who received his PhD from SOAS University of London (circa 1976–1981). He served as a lecturer at the University of Milan (circa 1993–2000) and held a post at the University of Bologna (circa 2002–2016).

Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard University (attested 2003) under the doctoral supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.

Eric Grinstead (1921–2008) worked in sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Victoria University of Wellington and held positions at the British Library (circa 1957–1970) and the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1969).
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Manchester and Uppsala, later serving as professor of the history of religion at Uppsala (1978–1981) and holding the first chair of religious studies at Sydney (1977–1996).

Eric M. Greene is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (2012) under Robert H. Sharf, and held a post as assistant professor of religious studies at Yale University (attested 2017).
Eric Reinders is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed MA degrees at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia (attested 2012), where he studied under Paul Groner.
Eric Teichman (1884–1944) was a scholar in Tibetology and sinology who studied at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, from circa 1904 to 1907.

Erica Baffelli (born 1976) specializes in Japanology and religious studies. She studied under Massimo Raveri (circa 1995–2004) and held posts at the University of Otago (circa 2009–2013) and the University of Manchester (attested 2013, 2018).

Erich Frauwallner (1898–1974) was an Austrian scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna (1918–1921), where he spent his academic career, serving as director and professor until becoming professor emeritus.

Erich Haenisch (1880–1966) was a scholar of sinology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. After studying under Wilhelm Grube at Humboldt University of Berlin, he held professorships at Göttingen (1925), Leipzig (circa 1925–1932), Berlin (1932), and Munich (1927–1951).

Erich Heintel (1912–2000) was a philosopher who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He served there as an extraordinary professor (1952) and ordinary professor of philosophy from 1960 to 1982.
